description:
FILED s543l (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-24): the residue of #2260 after s543l made a handler's die leave a blocking read (the reviewing session's ruling of 2026-11-24, option (b)).

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 | ./runpcl on the s543l tree):
    my ($in, $out); pipe $in, $out; my $line = 'untouched';
    eval { local $SIG{ALRM} = sub { die "abort\n" }; alarm 1; $line = readline $in; alarm 0 };
    print "line=[$line]\n";
  perl: line=[]           (pp_readline has set the TARGET to "" before the read blocks)
  PCL:  line=[untouched]  (the die leaves the read before the assignment; on the base the die was SWALLOWED and the
                           read returned undef, which printed like perl's "")

WHY RARE: the idiom's contract is the control flow and $@ (perlfunc alarm), which are right since s543l; the target's
value after a timed-out read is "" (DEFINED) in perl, so `defined $line` cannot tell a timeout from an empty read --
no program relies on it.  Pinned by the CANARY row 12b of Pl/t/fileio-02.t (it asserts today's 'untouched' and fails
the day this is fixed: then put `line=` back into row 12 and delete the canary).

DIRECTION (option (c) of #2260): a readline that knows its target -- the emission of `$x = <FH>` / `$x = readline FH`
passes the target so the read sets it to "" before it blocks, as pp_readline does.  It changes the emission of every
such site for a value read only after a timed-out read: measure the cost before building.
frequency_reason: the value a timed-out read leaves in its target: perl gives "" (defined), so no program can use it to detect the timeout -- programs test $@ (perlfunc alarm); known only from Pl/t/fileio-02.t row 12 and probes
subject: SILENT WRONG (rare): a readline interrupted by a dying signal handler leaves its TARGET as it was (`$line = <$fh>` under alarm: PCL 'untouched', perl "") -- the residue of #2260 after s543l
triage_reason: the target of a timed-out readline
